messages.author: 8d587ec0858ae795
messages.subject: Knit pdf(beamer) image include
parts:
Hi,
I am working in RStudio. I want to include in my .Rmd file some external png picture.

Before when I wrote stuff in Latex it was quite easy by \includegraphics{}

Not pretty sure how to manage it now...

Any help?

Regards

messages.author: 2710b717e5dbb066
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Knit pdf(beamer) image include
parts:
In general knitr will just pass LaTeX commands through to the .tex file for later processing, so you should be able to use the same \includegraphics command in your .Rmd file as you would use writing LaTeX directly.  

Have you tried this? did it work? not work? give an error?

If you can give us more detail on what you tried and how it did not work (or worked differently than expected) the easier it is for us to help you.

See fortune(324).

parts:
When I try :

```{r echo=FALSE}

\includegraphics[scale=0.5]{Economist1.png}

```

I get error:

Error in parse(text = x, srcfile = src) : <text>:2:1: unexpected input
1: 
2: \
   ^
Calls: <Anonymous> ... evaluate -> parse_all -> parse_all.character -> parse
Execution halted


When I use simply:

## Section

\includegraphics[scale=0.5]{Economist1.png}

I get error:

! LaTeX Error: File `Economist1' not found.

See the LaTeX manual or LaTeX Companion for explanation.
Type  H <return>  for immediate help.

when still image file is in working folder getwd()

messages.author: 2710b717e5dbb066
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Knit pdf(beamer) image include
parts:
The second option is where you want to go, the LaTeX commands should not be inside of an R block.

My guess is that you are dealing with an active directory/path issue, when you run LaTeX it is not finding your .png file because it is looking in the wrong place.  One simple option is to fully specify the path to Economist1.png.  Otherwise you need to figure out where knitr is running (possibly in a temporary directory) and either move the file there, or use the proper relative path.
